params.name: cor
params.let: 'It is a function, because each element of X appears exactly once as a first projection.' if t == 0 else 'It is not a function, because one element of X appears as the first projection of two different pairs.'

params.name: d1
params.let: 'It is not a function, because not every element of Y is used as a second projection.' if t == 0 else 'It is a function, because every ordered pair has a different second projection.'

params.name: d2
params.let: 'It is not a function, because no two pairs have the same second projection.' if t == 0 else 'It is a function, because all the ordered pairs are different from each other.'

params.name: s2
params.let: 'Each element of X appears exactly once as a first projection, so the relation is a function.' if t == 0 else 'One element of X appears twice as a first projection (and another element of X does not appear at all), so the relation is not a function.'

stem: Let $X=\{ {=x1}, {=x2}, {=x3}, {=x4}\}$ and $Y=\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9\}$. The relation $R$ from $X$ to $Y$ is given by the ordered pairs $R=\{({=x1}, {=y1}), ({=x2}, {=y2}), ({=x3}, {=y3}), ({=f4}, {=y4})\}$. Which statement is correct?
solution: The first projections of the ordered pairs are {=x1}, {=x2}, {=x3} and {=f4}.
The elements of X are {=x1}, {=x2}, {=x3} and {=x4}. A relation from X to Y is a function when each element of X appears exactly once as a first projection.

distractors.text: It cannot be decided without an arrow diagram.

proposed_misconceptions.label: Requires every element of Y to be used
proposed_misconceptions.description: Thinks a function must use every element of the co-domain as a second projection.

proposed_misconceptions.label: Checks second projections instead of first
proposed_misconceptions.description: Judges the relation by whether the second projections repeat or differ, rather than checking that each element of X appears once as a first projection.

notes: No book question was supplied; parent id is a placeholder. t=0: function. t=1: first projection of 4th pair repeats x1 and x4 is missing. ys are distinct so the pairs are always distinct and second projections never repeat.
